requirement_text: We accept secondary school diplomas which are equivalent to the Dutch VWO: the Dutch secondary school diploma which gives access to research universities. Is your diploma not listed here? The best way to figure out whether you are eligible for the program of your choice, is by submitting an application.
scope: Applicants with a non-Dutch educational background (the page routes Dutch-diploma holders to a separate national-procedure page).
researcher_notes: Captured via direct browser page-text extraction (raw DOM read, not an AI-summarising fetch). tilburguniversity.edu ends in .edu, so this and every other tilburguniversity.edu-sourced record in this batch passes looksOfficial() unlike most continental-European sources in this research wave.

requirement_text: Foundation (year) programs will not be accepted for admission.
researcher_notes: NAMED EXCLUSION: a completed university-foundation-year certificate, which numerically/structurally resembles a bridging qualification, is explicitly not an accepted admission pathway at Tilburg even though other one-year bridging routes (see companion bridging-pathway record) are accepted.

requirement_text: VWO (pre-university) diploma. Are you applying with a Dutch educational background? You can find more information about application and admission on our webpage in Dutch.
scope: Reference entry on the international-diploma page; the page itself routes actual Dutch-diploma applicants to a separate Dutch-language procedure.
researcher_notes: Extracted from the page's per-country accordion list via DOM inspection (the accordion panel content is present in the HTML but collapsed/hidden by CSS; innerText on the closed <details> element returns only the summary heading, so outerHTML/innerHTML was read directly rather than relying on visible-text extraction). This same technique was used for every country accordion cited in this batch (Turkey, IB, UK, USA, Germany, and the 'not directly eligible' group).

requirement_text: International Baccalaureate diploma: Tilburg University only accepts the full International Baccalaureate Diploma, which includes the core (Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and CAS) and subjects taken from groups 1-5 or groups 1-6 - of which at least three subjects must be at Higher Level. The overall score must be ≥ 24. Individual diploma program course results are not accepted for admission purposes. Please note: Predicted grades are not used for the evaluation.
limitations: No minimum HL-subject grade figures are stated on this page, only the overall-score floor (≥24) and the core/HL-count structural requirements.
researcher_notes: NAMED EXCLUSION: 'individual diploma program course results are not accepted' — a candidate who only completed some IB courses (not the full diploma with core) does not qualify, even if the completed subjects individually meet Higher Level standards. This is the same shape as the recency/named-exclusion traps documented in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md: a numerically-strong partial record does not satisfy the rule as published.

requirement_text: Lise diplomasi with a Diploma Puani (Notu) of at least 85% from a Genel Lise. The Imam-Hatip Lise Diplomasi, Meslek Lisesi Diplomasi and Teknik Lisesi Diplomasi will not be considered for direct admission. Students attending a private, international school following an International Baccalaureate curriculum are referred to the International Baccalaureate diploma requirements.
researcher_notes: Directly relevant to ORYN's Turkey focus. NAMED EXCLUSION: only a Genel Lise (general/academic high school) diploma qualifies for direct admission at ≥85%. Imam-Hatip Lisesi, Meslek Lisesi (vocational) and Teknik Lisesi (technical) diplomas — all real, common Turkish secondary-school tracks — are explicitly named as NOT accepted for direct admission even if the grade is high, mirroring the Turkey-diploma exclusion pattern TU Delft also documents for its own country list (see de_nl_requirements_delft file, DEL0006, though the named excluded categories differ by institution). A Turkish IB-track student is routed instead to the separate IB rule (see companion IB record); a companion note on the same source panel also requires that IB course names/levels be listed clearly on the TiU Statement of Educational Institution form, with predicted IB grades not used for evaluation.

requirement_text: At least 3 GCE accepted A-levels in general academic subjects with grades A*-C, plus 3 GCSE academic subjects with grades A*-C or 4-9 (six different subjects in total). Accepted A levels: Biology, Chemistry, Classical Civilisation, Economics, English (a combination of Language and Literature will be considered as one A-level subject), Geography, Government and Politics, Further Mathematics (a combination of Mathematics and Further Mathematics will be considered as one A-level subject), History, Languages (not your native tongue other than English), Mathematics, Philosophy, Physics, Psychology, Religion and Sociology. Two of the above accepted A-level subjects plus another subject not listed, such as Business studies may also be considered. These applications will be considered on a case-by-case basis and depend on the appropriacy of the subject, grade achieved (minimum score B for all 3 subjects), and the selected Bachelor program.
limitations: No minimum total UCAS-tariff-style points figure is stated; Tilburg gates on grade letters and named subjects, not a points score.
researcher_notes: NAMED-SUBJECT CASE-BY-CASE RULE: a case not on the accepted-subjects list (e.g. Business Studies) is not automatically rejected but requires a stricter grade floor (minimum B, versus C for listed subjects) and is evaluated case-by-case — a numeric-only checker would need to distinguish 'on named list, grade C ok' from 'off named list, grade B minimum' rather than applying one threshold.

requirement_text: American High School diploma from an accredited high school with at least 4 College Board Advanced Placement examinations (not accepted are: AP Capstone, AP Research, AP Seminar, AP Precalculus and AP Studio Art) with a minimum score of 3.
researcher_notes: NAMED EXCLUSION: 5 specific AP exam titles (AP Capstone, AP Research, AP Seminar, AP Precalculus, AP Studio Art) do not count toward the required 4 AP exams even though they are real, transcript-listed College Board AP exams with numeric scores. A student holding 4 AP scores of 5 where one of the four is AP Precalculus would, on Tilburg's own wording, not meet this requirement as published — a threshold-only check (count of APs ≥ 4, score ≥ 3) would wrongly pass this case.

requirement_text: Zeugnis der Allgemeinen Hochschulreife
limitations: This is the complete text of Tilburg's Germany accordion entry — just the diploma name, with no Leistungskurs/Grundkurs subject-level detail. Contrast with TU Delft's Germany entry (see de_nl_requirements_delft, DEL0008), which specifies Mathematik at LK/erhöhtem Anforderungsniveau and other named subjects. Tilburg's general Mathematics-requirements page (see companion math records) separately layers a mathematics condition on top of this diploma for math-requiring programs, but no other subject-specific Abitur condition was found stated for Germany on Tilburg's pages checked in this pass.

requirement_text: Students with a secondary education diploma from the following countries cannot be admitted directly because the level is not equivalent to the Dutch Pre-University education (VWO), and must instead pursue the 'Not directly eligible' bridging pathway: Brazil, Chile, China, Ecuador, Indonesia, Morocco, Peru, the Russian Federation, and South Korea.
limitations: Each of the 9 countries has its own near-identical accordion entry on the source page using boilerplate wording very close to: 'Students with a secondary education diploma from [Country] cannot be admitted directly because the level is not equivalent to the Dutch Pre-University education (called ‘VWO’ in Dutch).' This record consolidates 9 separately-fetched, near-duplicate accordion panels into one list rather than 9 near-identical rows; marked extracted_summary because the country list is a researcher-compiled aggregation even though each individual source sentence is close to verbatim. This list is drawn only from the ~65 countries whose accordions were opened in this pass and is very likely not exhaustive of all countries where this applies.
researcher_notes: Directly actionable for ORYN: a student from any of these 9 countries needs the bridging-pathway record (see companion record) rather than direct application, regardless of grades.

requirement_text: The diploma requirements below might differ for the Joint Bachelor's program in Data Science. The application and admission procedure for this joint program is done exclusively via Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e). You cannot, nor should you apply via both universities.
limitations: This record only carries Tilburg's own cross-reference notice. The actual Data Science diploma requirements were not independently fetched from TU/e's own site in this pass (out of scope: this lane covers tilburguniversity.edu only). See companion record TIL0046 for the fuller authority note on this joint program.
researcher_notes: SCOPE WARNING: any general Tilburg diploma/math/English rule in this batch should NOT be assumed to apply unmodified to BSc Data Science; this same carve-out recurs on the math-requirements and English-proficiency pages (see companion records TIL0019, TIL0022).

requirement_text: If you are not directly eligible for our programs: (1) Complete one year at a Dutch university of applied sciences, preferably in a study program related to the program you want to study at Tilburg University, and pass all the courses offered; with the propaedeutic certificate you receive, you can reapply for entry into our Bachelor's programs. OR (2) Complete one year in an academic program at a research university in your home country, closely related to your Bachelor's program of choice; the entire first-year curriculum needs to be completed with sufficient scores, with the exact level and value depending on the institution, study content, nominal duration and GPA. Be aware that additional requirements may still apply, such as passing a Mathematics test or achieving a certain grade point average.
limitations: Combines two separate bullet-point pathway options from the source's 'Not directly eligible?' section into one record; each option is close to verbatim individually but this record merges both, hence extracted_summary rather than verbatim_quoted. Neither pathway has a stated numeric GPA/score threshold on this page — both defer to 'sufficient scores' / case-by-case assessment.
researcher_notes: Confirmed independently worded but substantively identical on the Bachelor's application-and-admission hub page's own 'Not directly eligible?' accordion.

requirement_text: IELTS Academic with a minimum total score of 6.0 and a minimum subscore of 5.5 on the Writing and Speaking sections of the test. Note: we do not accept IELTS Online.
scope: Bachelor's programs (default; Data Science has different requirements — see companion record).
researcher_notes: NAMED EXCLUSION: IELTS Online is explicitly not accepted regardless of the band score achieved — same shape as the Koc/Edinburgh provenance-exclusion pattern in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT - test reports obtained on or after January 21, 2026: minimum total score of 4 and minimum subscores of 4 for Writing and 3 for Speaking.
scope: Bachelor's programs (default; Data Science has different requirements — see companion record).
researcher_notes: Correctly handles the ETS 21 January 2026 rescale exactly as scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md's 'resolved' case describes: explicitly dated to ETS's own real effective date, on the new 1-6 scale, with both an overall and per-section minimum. Captured via direct browser page-text extraction, not an AI-summarising fetch.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT - test reports obtained before January 21, 2026: minimum total score of 80 and minimum subscores of 19 for Writing and 17 for Speaking.
scope: Bachelor's programs (default; Data Science has different requirements — see companion record).
limitations: Bounded to its own stated date range (before 21 Jan 2026), so unambiguous for test reports issued in that window, matching Edinburgh's pre-cutover TOEFL row and TU Delft's legacy MSc TOEFL row in the companion trap document/corpus.
researcher_notes: Captured via direct browser page-text extraction.

requirement_text: The test must be taken at a test center. We only accept TOEFL iBT Home Edition scores in exceptional circumstances, such as when on-site test centers are closed or inaccessible due to unsafe conditions in a country.
researcher_notes: NAMED PROVENANCE RULE: applies to all three accepted tests generically ('all English tests must be taken at an authorized exam center'), with TOEFL Home Edition singled out as the one narrow, conditional exception. Independently confirmed on the Master's English-requirements FAQ (see companion Master's record), which states the identical exception in near-identical wording.

requirement_text: Cambridge English test results: C1 advanced (formerly CAE) or C2 proficiency (formerly CPE): with a minimum total score of 169 and a minimum subscore of 162 for Writing and Speaking. The minimum required Cambridge level is below the official Cambridge Advanced pass mark, but is in line with comparable tests and therefore accepted for admission.
scope: Bachelor's programs (default; Data Science has different requirements — see companion record).
researcher_notes: Tilburg explicitly self-discloses that its accepted score (169) sits below the official Cambridge Advanced pass mark — a rare case of an institution documenting, in its own words, that its bar is a deliberately lowered/adapted threshold rather than the test operator's own pass standard. Worth preserving verbatim rather than just recording '169' as a bare number.

requirement_text: The test results must be no older than two years prior to the start of the academic year. You must be able to demonstrate your English language proficiency at the time of application. Without test results your application cannot be processed unless you are exempted.
limitations: RECENCY RULE (same shape as Edinburgh's qualification-age constraint and TU Delft's certificate-age rule documented in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md): two independent conditions are stated — (a) the test itself must be ≤2 years old relative to the START OF THE ACADEMIC YEAR, and (b) proof must exist AT THE TIME OF APPLICATION (a separate, earlier checkpoint). An evaluator needs the test date, the application submission date, and the academic-year start date to check this correctly; a single 'is score present' check is insufficient. Independently corroborated verbatim in the FAQ accordion 'Can I apply first and send in my IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge results after?': 'No, you must be able to demonstrate your English language proficiency at the time of application. Without test results your application cannot be processed.'

requirement_text: We do not accept a combination of test results on different test dates, such as TOEFL's 'My Best Scores' and IELTS 1 skill retake.
limitations: NAMED EXCLUSION, same Koc-superscore/Glasgow-provenance shape as scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md: a numerically-qualifying composite built from TOEFL MyBest Scores or an IELTS One Skill Retake is rejected on provenance, not on the number itself. NOTABLE CROSS-INSTITUTION CONTRAST: TU Delft's own Master's English-proficiency page explicitly ACCEPTS 'IELTS One Skill Retake' ('IELTS One Skill Retake will be accepted... The IELTS Online (Academic) test and the IELTS Indicator test cannot be accepted' — see de_nl_requirements_delft, DEL0027), the opposite policy to Tilburg's. Two official Dutch university sources genuinely disagree on this specific provenance rule; both are recorded as found, neither silently reconciled, per this lane's conflict-handling rule.

requirement_text: The minimum English proficiency requirements for the Bachelor's program in Data Science differ. For more information, please check the admission and application webpage of Data Science.
limitations: The actual differing Data Science thresholds were not found on tilburguniversity.edu in this pass; Data Science's own Tilburg admission page defers entirely to TU/e (see TIL0046). Do not apply the general IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge numbers in TIL0012-0016 to Data Science applicants.

requirement_text: English proficiency test results are not required if: you completed your entire secondary education in English (with the exemption of home schooling and online education) in one of the following countries: Australia, Canada (with the exception of Quebec), Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, or the United States of America. OR you have an International Baccalaureate (IB) diploma with English as the language of instruction, a European Baccalaureate (EB) diploma with English 1 or English 2, or Cambridge International GCSE and A Levels. OR your high school diploma is one of a listed set of national diplomas (Dutch/Surinam/Antillean VWO; Austrian Reife(prüfungs)zeugnis; Belgian ASO; Danish Studentereksamenbevis/Bevis for Høgjere Forberedelseksamen; Finnish Ylioppilastutkintotodistus/Studentexamensbevis; French Diploma du Baccalauréate Général option OIB English or option BFI section Anglais; German Zeugnis der Allgemeinen Hochschulreife; Hungarian Erettsegi Bizonyitvany from a General Gymnazium; Latvian Atestats par Visparejo Videjo Izglitibu; Lithuanian Brandos Atestatas from a Gimnazija/Licejus; Luxembourg Diplôme de fin d'études secondaires - classique; Maltese Matriculation Certificate; Norwegian Vitnemål fra den vidergaonde skolen up to Vg3; Romanian Diploma de Bacalauret - filiere teoretica; Slovak Vysvedcenie o Maturitnej skuske from a Gymnazium; Swedish Slutbetyg fran Gymnasieskolan) AND English was one of the examination subjects on that diploma.
limitations: Most named diplomas carry an asterisk on the source page marking 'a pass for English as part of the examination subjects' as a condition; this record folds that condition into the running text rather than reproducing the asterisk footnote mechanism. See companion record TIL0021 for a hard override on this entire exemption list.
researcher_notes: Captured via direct browser page-text extraction.

requirement_text: Please note: prospective students who are interested in the Bachelor's program in Data Science are not exempted. An English proficiency test is required.
researcher_notes: NAMED EXCLUSION that inverts an otherwise-broad rule: this overrides EVERY exemption route in TIL0020 (nationality, IB/EB/Cambridge, and the full named-diploma list) specifically for Data Science applicants. A US-national applicant with a US high school diploma, who would be exempt for every other Tilburg Bachelor's program, still needs an English test score for Data Science. A checker that only consulted the general exemption list would wrongly exempt this applicant.

requirement_text: Some Bachelor's programs require applied or advanced knowledge of mathematics. In case you are interested in one of the following Bachelor's programs you must provide proof of your mathematics proficiency: Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Econometrics and Operations Research, Economics, Entrepreneurship and Business Innovation, Global Management of Social Issues, Human Resource Studies: People Management, International Business Administration, International Sociology, Psychology. Please note that you need to obtain a passing grade for the Mathematics course in your final exam. The Mathematics requirements might differ for the Joint Bachelor's program in Data Science; the application and admission procedure for this joint program is done exclusively via Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e).
researcher_notes: Overview record; see companion OMPT-tier records (TIL0023-0025) for the actual per-program numeric thresholds used when a diploma's own mathematics course does not directly satisfy this.

requirement_text: OMPT (Online Mathematics Placement Test) requirement for Economics, Entrepreneurship and Business Innovation, and International Business Administration: OMPT-A with a minimum score of 70%, maximum two attempts to reach the minimum passing score. The same OMPT-A test and 70% threshold also applies to Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence.
scope: Applicants whose diploma does not already directly satisfy the program's mathematics requirement; used for the Boswell-Beta/CCVX/OMPT bridging exam route (see companion record).
limitations: Source presents this as two separate small tables ('Economics and Management' field and 'Humanities and Digital Sciences' field) rather than prose; this record flattens 4 identical-threshold table rows (Economics, Econometrics... no — Econometrics and Operations Research uses OMPT-D, see companion record — Entrepreneurship and Business Innovation, International Business Administration, Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence) into one combined record with program_name left null, mirroring TU Delft's DEL0035 portfolio-grouping precedent, rather than 4 near-duplicate rows.
researcher_notes: Attempt cap ('maximum two attempts to reach the minimum passing score') is itself a named constraint beyond the bare percentage — a 3rd-attempt pass would not, on this wording, count.

requirement_text: OMPT-D with a minimum score of 70%, maximum two attempts to reach the minimum passing score.
scope: Applicants whose diploma does not already directly satisfy the program's mathematics requirement.
researcher_notes: The only Bachelor's program in this source table requiring the OMPT-D variant specifically rather than OMPT-A — consistent with Econometrics and Operations Research being the most mathematics-intensive of Tilburg's Economics-cluster programs.

requirement_text: OMPT-A with a minimum score of 60% for Global Management of Social Issues, Human Resource Studies: People Management, International Sociology, and Psychology. The Mathematics requirement for these Social and Behavioral Sciences programs is equivalent to Havo Mathematics A or B level. In general the level of mathematics will be sufficient if you have taken mathematics as an examination subject in your final year of high school (the diploma needs to be equivalent to the Dutch VWO diploma) and you received a passing grade.
scope: Applicants whose diploma does not already directly satisfy the program's mathematics requirement.
limitations: Combines 4 identical-threshold table rows (60%, no stated attempt cap unlike the 70% tier) with the source's separate explanatory paragraph about Havo-level equivalence; program_name left null per the same grouping rationale as TIL0023.
researcher_notes: NOTE: no 'maximum two attempts' language is stated for this 60% tier, unlike the 70% tier in TIL0023/TIL0024 — recorded as found rather than assumed to carry over.

requirement_text: If you don't meet the mathematic requirements you will receive a conditional admission letter stating that you need to take an additional mathematics exam. Training and exams can be taken at the Boswell-Beta Institute or Centrale Commissie Voortentamen (CCVX). Students with an international diploma living abroad can take the Online Mathematics Placement Test (OMPT). You must submit the obtained certificate before the start of the program.
limitations: The submission cutoff is 'before the start of the program' — tied to each cycle's own start date rather than a fixed calendar date, so no deadline record was created from this fact (does not fit the deadline_date/recurrence contract cleanly).

requirement_text: You can apply to our study programs at any time and will receive a decision on your (conditional) admission within 4 to 6 weeks. We evaluate applications as they come in, rather than waiting for a deadline. While applying early won't increase your chances of being accepted, we recommend applying as soon as possible... Note: Psychology follows a selection procedure instead of rolling admission.
researcher_notes: NAMED EXCLUSION: Psychology is explicitly carved out of the 'apply any time, rolling decision' model because of its numerus fixus selection procedure (see deadline records and TIL0029). All other Bachelor's programs, including the other early/extended-deadline ones (Data Science, Digital Culture and Society, Liberal Arts and Sciences), remain rolling-admission within their respective deadlines.

requirement_text: You need to upload a number of documents in pdf-format: Copy Passport / ID card to verify your identity; Secondary / Higher Education school diploma (or a Statement of Educational Institution if not yet obtained); Official grade lists issued by your school and/or academic advisor. A sworn translator must translate the documents (accepted languages are Dutch, German, French, or English). They need to be certified with a stamp and signature. If you are conditionally accepted to the program, you will be required to send us certified copies of your documents.
scope: Bachelor's programs, Step 1 of the application process.
researcher_notes: NAMED LANGUAGE CONSTRAINT: sworn-translator translations are accepted only in Dutch, German, French, or English — a certified translation into a fifth language would not satisfy this as published.

requirement_text: Before you start your program, we'd like to help you find out if your preferred program is a good match. The matching activity helps you assess whether the program aligns with your interests and meets your expectations. This activity can involve an interview, an (online) assessment, or attending an (online) lecture. The advice is non-binding, so independent to your admission to the study program. Exceptions: For Psychology, a selection procedure (numerus fixus) applies, meaning there is no matching process. For Liberal Arts and Sciences (a selective program without numerus fixus), matching is also not offered; instead, you take part in a mandatory admissions interview in which the outcome is binding.
researcher_notes: Sharp distinction to preserve: for most Bachelor's programs the matching-activity outcome is explicitly NON-BINDING and separate from admission, while for Liberal Arts and Sciences the analogous interview outcome is explicitly BINDING — the same general concept ('an interview happens') has opposite consequences depending on the program. See companion record TIL0030 for LAS's own page confirming this.

program_name: University College Tilburg: Liberal Arts and Sciences
requirement_text: Liberal Arts and Sciences is a selective program. The application procedure consists of two phases. In the first phase we check your eligibility; in the second phase we assess whether you and the program are a good fit on the basis of an application form and an interview. A positive decision at the end of both phases is required to be able to get admitted to the program.
researcher_notes: Confirmed on the program's own dedicated admission page, corroborating the hub-page accordion summary (TIL0029). A positive eligibility check ALONE is not sufficient — the interview-based fit assessment is a second, independently-gating phase.

requirement_text: You can apply for a maximum of 4 programs at the same time at different universities within the Netherlands and a maximum two Numerus Fixus programs at the same time in Studielink.
limitations: This is Tilburg's own restatement of a Studielink platform-wide registration rule, not independently verified directly on studielink.nl in this pass (only the numerus-fixus/non-fixus deadline dates were independently checked on studielink.nl — see deadlines file).
researcher_notes: Contrast with the Master's page, which states only the 4-program cap with no separate numerus-fixus sub-cap (see companion Master's record TIL0044) — recorded as found, not assumed symmetric.

requirement_text: IELTS Academic: minimum total score of 6.5 and a minimum subscore of 6.0 on the Writing and Speaking sections of the test. We do not accept IELTS Online.
scope: Master's programs (default; individual programs with GRE/GMAT or other requirements layer additional conditions).
researcher_notes: Master's-level IELTS bar (6.5/6.0) is higher than the Bachelor's-level bar (6.0/5.5, see TIL0012) — consistent with a Master's threshold generally exceeding the Bachelor's threshold, the same pattern TU Delft shows for its own Cambridge scores.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT - test reports obtained on or after January 21, 2026: minimum total score of 4.5 and minimum subscores of 4.5 for Writing and 4 for Speaking.
researcher_notes: Correctly dated to ETS's real 21 Jan 2026 cutover, on the new 1-6 scale. Master's threshold (4.5/4.5/4) exceeds the Bachelor's threshold (4/4/3, see TIL0013) on the same new scale.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT - test reports obtained before January 21, 2026: minimum total score of 90 and minimum subscores of 22 for Writing and 21 for Speaking.
limitations: Bounded to its own stated date range (before 21 Jan 2026), so unambiguous for reports issued in that window.

requirement_text: All tests must be taken at an authorized test center, we do not accept online versions of tests such as IELTS Online. The only exception is the TOEFL iBT Home Edition, which we accept under special circumstances, such as when on-site language test centers are closed or inaccessible due to unsafe conditions in a country.
researcher_notes: Corroborates TIL0015 (Bachelor's) independently via the Master's FAQ accordion 'Do you accept English language test results of online tests, such as the TOEFL IBT Home Edition?' — same policy at both levels.

requirement_text: Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency: minimum total score of 176 and a minimum subscore of 169 for Writing and Speaking. The minimum required Cambridge level is below the official Cambridge Advanced pass mark, but is in line with comparable tests and therefore accepted for admission.
researcher_notes: Master's-level Cambridge bar (176/169) exceeds the Bachelor's-level bar (169/162, see TIL0016); note the Master's subscore floor (169) equals the Bachelor's TOTAL floor (169) — easy to misread if the two levels' numbers are seen out of context.

requirement_text: The test results must be no older than two years prior to the start of the academic year. You need to have proof of English proficiency at the time of application. Your application will only be considered if you include English test results that meet our requirements.
limitations: RECENCY RULE, identical anchor structure to the Bachelor's rule (TIL0017): ≤2 years relative to start of academic year, AND proof required at time of application. Corroborated in FAQ: 'The English language test results are a mandatory part of your application. Without results that meet our requirements, your application will not be considered.'
researcher_notes: CONTRAST with the GRE/GMAT recency rule on this same page (see TIL0039), which anchors its 2-year window to 'time of application' only, not 'start of academic year' — two different recency anchors for two different test types on the same admissions page.

requirement_text: Some programs in the field of business and economics require minimum GRE or GMAT scores for admission. GMAT Exam (Focus Edition): minimum total score of 525.
limitations: This general admission-and-application page does not name which specific Master's programs require GRE/GMAT; it states the requirement applies to 'some programs in the field of business and economics' and defers program-level specifics to each program's own page, which were not individually fetched in this pass. Confidence set to medium because the applicability scope (which exact programs) is not resolved here, though the score threshold itself is a direct verbatim quote.

requirement_text: GRE: minimum GRE score required varies by program. Please refer to the specific program pages for detailed information. The GRE institution code for Tilburg University is 0730. It is not obligatory to have completed the GMAT/GRE test before application. In our online application system you can indicate the approximate test date. If you don't have the results at the time of application, you must have them before the start of your studies by August 31 (Fall intake) or January 31 (Spring intake) for unconditional admission to a Master's program. The certificate(s) must not be older than two years at the time of application.
limitations: No specific GRE score threshold is given on this general page (deferred to individual program pages, not fetched in this pass); the institution code and timing/recency rules are direct quotes and high-confidence, but the numeric score bar itself is not resolved here. RECENCY RULE with a DIFFERENT anchor than the English-test recency rule on this same page (TIL0037): here the 2-year window is measured from 'time of application', not 'start of the academic year' — exactly the anchor-ambiguity trap scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md warns about.
researcher_notes: See companion deadline records (Aug 31 Fall / Jan 31 Spring) for the unconditional-admission cutoff dates this text describes.

requirement_text: Students who have completed a (relevant) degree at a Tilburg School of Economics and Management official partner university are exempted from taking the GRE/GMAT.
scope: Selected Master's programs in business/economics requiring GRE/GMAT.
limitations: The specific list of TiSEM 'official partner universities' was not independently fetched in this pass (linked from this page but not followed) — this record only confirms the exemption rule exists, not which institutions qualify.

requirement_text: To be eligible to start the (pre-)Master's program, your Bachelor's degree must be fully completed as legally required by the 'Bachelor-before-Master-rule'. If you finish your Bachelor's degree by completing your final course or defending your thesis but receive your diploma later, you can provide a Graduation Statement from your institution confirming you've met all requirements and the diploma award date, with an original seal/stamp and signature. We can temporarily accept this document until you receive your diploma, but it must be submitted by August 31 (Fall semester) or January 31 (Spring semester). If you have outstanding credits after this date, the statement will not be accepted.
researcher_notes: NAMED CONDITION: the Graduation Statement is explicitly a temporary substitute, not equivalent to a diploma — it stops being accepted if 'outstanding credits' remain after the Aug 31/Jan 31 cutoff, i.e. a Statement confirming '99% complete, thesis pending' does not satisfy the rule after that date. See companion deadline records for the Aug 31/Jan 31 dates.

requirement_text: If you have a non-Dutch diploma, you cannot apply directly for a pre-Master's program. If you apply for the Master's program, your application will automatically be considered for admission to both the Master's and pre-Master's program.
limitations: Not all Master's programs offer a pre-Master's route; this record only confirms the application-channel rule for those that do.

requirement_text: If you have an HBO (Dutch university of applied sciences) Bachelor's degree, you need to complete a pre-Master's program before you can start a Master's. You must follow the national application procedure and deadlines. If you do not have a valid Dutch residence permit at the time your studies are expected to start, you must apply using the non-EEA deadline instead.
limitations: SCOPE CARVE-OUT: this population (HBO Bachelor's holders) is explicitly routed OUT of the international procedure this batch otherwise researched, and into a separate 'national procedure' whose deadlines were not independently fetched in this pass — the general international Master's deadlines in this file (TIL0013-0016 in the deadlines file) do not apply to this group.

requirement_text: You can apply for a maximum of 4 programs at the same time at different universities within the Netherlands.
researcher_notes: Unlike the Bachelor's page (TIL0031), no separate numerus-fixus sub-cap is stated here for Master's; recorded as found, not assumed symmetric with the Bachelor's rule.

requirement_text: A selection procedure applies for the academic year of 2026-2027. There are 120 places available for the Master's (track) Clinical Neuropsychology. This selection takes place based on the Regulations for Selection and Admission Master's program Psychologie en Geestelijke Gezondheid. Candidates who have received a ranking number between 0-120 will be selected; candidates ranked above 120 are placed on a waiting list. You can apply for one track of the Master program Psychologie en Geestelijke Gezondheid (Clinical Neuropsychology, Klinische Kinder- en Jeugdpsychologie, Klinische Psychologie, or Klinische Forensische Psychologie). It is not possible to be selected for multiple tracks. If you have applied for multiple tracks in Studielink, be sure to withdraw your application for the third and possibly fourth track by January 15, 2026 23:59 CET.
limitations: The 2026-2027 selection cycle's own withdraw-by deadline (January 15, 2026) has already passed as of retrieval (2026-08-21). Tilburg's page still frames this as 'the academic year of 2026-2027' with no visible staleness notice; unlike TU Delft's equivalent CSE page, it does not self-identify as showing a closed/previous cycle. Kept deliberately per this lane's VERIFIED_HISTORICAL convention rather than dropped; do not treat the 120-place figure or ranking mechanics as confirmed-current for the next (2027-2028) cycle without a freshness recheck.
researcher_notes: NAMED CONSTRAINT: only ONE of four tracks within the same Master's program may be pursued to selection; applying to multiple tracks in Studielink requires an affirmative withdrawal action by the same Jan 15 deadline or the application is presumably left in an inconsistent state (not explicitly stated what happens if not withdrawn).

requirement_text: The BSc Data Science is a joint program of Tilburg University and Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e). The application and admission procedure is done exclusively via TU/e. You cannot, nor should you apply via both universities. Once you have completed your enrollment at TU/e, you will automatically be enrolled at Tilburg University. This page contains a brief overview of the application process for the BSc Data Science. For the complete information we refer you to the website of Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e). In all cases, the information on the TU/e website is leading.
limitations: AUTHORITY NOTE: Tilburg's own page explicitly subordinates itself to TU/e's website ('the information on the TU/e website is leading') for this specific joint program. Every Data Science-scoped record in this batch (TIL0010, TIL0019, TIL0021, TIL0022 partial) is Tilburg's own restatement/cross-reference only; TU/e's own site (tue.nl) was not fetched in this pass — out of scope for a Tilburg-exclusive research lane. Any ingestion of Data Science requirements should treat tue.nl, not tilburguniversity.edu, as primary once available.
